summary: Remote WebSocket-controlled agent grants full shell, filesystem, and self-upgrade control over installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent installs and runs as a background service that connects to a configurable WebSocket server (default ws://localhost:3456) and exposes a broad remote-control surface driven by unsolicited messages from that server. On `terminal_create` the agent spawns a PTY running the user's default shell (bash on Linux/macOS, powershell/cmd on Windows) and pipes subsequent `terminal_input` messages from the server directly into the PTY, streaming output back — arbitrary command execution on the host as the agent user. The same message router accepts server-initiated `read_file`, `write_file`, `delete_files`, `move`, `copy`, directory listing, git add/reset/restore/commit/push, HTTP/WebSocket proxy, and filesystem-search operations, giving the remote peer full read/write access to files reachable by the agent and the ability to pivot network traffic through the host. An `upgrade_agent` message causes the agent to fetch @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest from the configured npm registry, install it, and respawn under systemd/launchd/PM2 — arbitrary new code from the registry is executed on the host on command. The Linux service installer also modifies PATH via shell RC to prepend ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin. The remote server URL is configurable, but nothing in the protocol restricts what a peer that reaches that endpoint can do: any party controlling or reaching that WebSocket endpoint obtains persistent full-host command execution, file access, and code-push capability against every machine running the agent.
